timeline: If your boat rides a seventeen-hundred-foot wave over the forest canopy on July 9, 1958, how do you manage to walk away alive?
In July nineteen fifty-eight, an earthquake shook loose forty million cubic yards of rock.
Howard Ulrich and his seven-year-old son watched from their small fishing boat as the water rose.
The impact sent a wall of water surging seventeen hundred feet up the mountainside.
Their boat was lifted high into the air by the massive swell and somehow survived.
You probably think coastal tsunamis max out at fifty feet, until you look at the tree line in Lituya Bay.
